headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Installing Cabinet Hardware
articleBody:
Installing new cabinet hardware is one of those small touches that can make a huge difference in your kitchen or bathroom remodel. But even this seemingly simple task can go awry if you're not careful. Avoiding common mistakes is key to achieving that clean, professional look and ensuring your hardware enhances functionality and beauty.

Common Mistakes to Avoid:

1.  Measuring from inconsistent reference points: Always establish a clear, consistent reference point—like the top corner or edge—for all your measurements to ensure hardware alignment. This prevents a misaligned, unprofessional appearance.
2.  Drilling before testing the layout: Never drill without first confirming your desired placement. Use a template, a jig, or even painter's tape to visualize the hardware's position on the cabinet door or drawer. This allows you to make adjustments before any permanent marks are made.
3.  Using the wrong screw length: Screws that are too long will protrude into the cabinet interior or even through the front, while screws that are too short won't hold the hardware securely. Always match the screw length to the combined thickness of your hardware and cabinet material.
4.  Drilling at an angle or allowing the bit to wander: A crooked drill hole can make hardware sit unevenly or be difficult to install. Use an awl to create a pilot dimple and a drill guide or jig to keep your drill bit straight and prevent damage to your cabinet fronts.
5.  Failing to use a backer board for delicate materials: When drilling through veneer, thin panels, or brittle coatings, place a scrap piece of wood behind the drilling location. This provides support and prevents unsightly tear-out or chipping on the cabinet's finish.
